articleTitle: Optimization and Management of Residential Energy Systems: Forecasting Methods, Energy Efficiency Models, and Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Residential energy management systems are crucial for optimizing energy consumption, reducing costs, and improving grid stability. Various optimization techniques have been proposed, including mixed integer linear programming and model predictive control. This paper, present literature on optimization and management of residential energy systems focusing on forecasting methods, energy efficiency models, and renewable integration. A systematic literature review on electrical loads in residential buildings was conducted using Scopus, yielding 31 relevant papers after filtering. VOSviewer analysis identified 37 keywords, organized into clusters to highlight research trends and gaps for further investigation. The literature results highlight innovative approaches and technologies for optimizing energy management in residential buildings. A noticeable aspect is the emphasis on using data-driven methods and advanced optimization techniques to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of energy systems. Future research possible areas to be explored are recommended in this paper.

articleTitle: Measures and Procedure for Implementation of Digitalization of Production at JSC «Qarmet»
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The article deals with the activities and procedure for implementing digitalization of production, within the framework of Industry 4.0, which implies increasing automation and intellectualization of all industrial production processes: from digital design of a product, creation of its digital copy, predictive maintenance in real time, automated component supply system to individualized approach in working with customers. Modern concepts of product quality are based on the principle of absolute satisfaction of customer recommendations. This is achieved by the introduction of automated process control and monitoring systems. The scientific novelty lies in the implementation of real-time systems that can analyze data and detect defects in real time, providing rapid response and minimizing scrap. The presence of surface defects is characteristic of hot rolling mill production. This article discusses the Isra Parsytec system for automatic inspection and identification of surface defects. Isra Parsytec systems are designed based on an IT architecture ready for use in the emerging Industrie 4.0 environment. Thanks to ISRA's modular hardware platform, the technical equipment can be easily scaled and customized for specific tasks in production. ISRA is utilizing a full range of technical solutions to ensure that machine vision systems comply with Industrie 4.0 and prepare for the opportunities offered by image processing in digital and networked manufacturing. The considered activities are carried out at the hot rolling mill, which are aimed at improving the quality of manufactured products within the framework of the 4th industrial revolution. Implementation of this system can realize the receipt of quality products and increase production performance. Data on surface defects can improve the technology of sheet production.

articleTitle: Self-Oscillating IPT System Based on Phase Tracking Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The coupling in an inductive power transfer (IPT) system make frequency tracking and power control difficult. This article presents an IPT system using a self-oscillation approach to solve this problem. In this system, the working period is divided into two stages: independent oscillating stage and power injecting stage. Based on these two stages, we established a closed loop to analyze the phase of the system. This loop is composed of three units to achieve phase tracking, power regulating and self-oscillating respectively. Self-oscillation will be realized in an IPT system by this loop. After the experiment verification, the implementation method for the system demonstrates effectiveness by tracking and compensating for system changes in a single cycle effectively.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Resistor-Loaded Metamaterial Absorber for ISM Bands Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: A dual-band, resistor-loaded metamaterial electromagnetic absorber that is polarization-independent and aimed for ISM band applications is presented in the current paper. The suggested metamaterial absorber's unit cell structure is composed of up of three dielectric layers, with an air layer positioned between two cost-effective FR-4 dielectric layers. On the top dielectric layer, two copper square rings are connected using four lumped resistors. The simulation findings show that at the lower (2.45 GHz) and higher (5.8 GHz) frequency bands, respectively, the proposed absorber achieved absorption rates of 99.43% and 99.22%. A sample of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> unit-cells absorber was fabricated and there is a robust link between simulation as well as measurement data. Moreover, the suggested dual-band absorber maintains effective performance across various polarization angles.

articleTitle: Applications in Smart Home Automation: Enhancing Security, Accessibility, and Efficiency Through IoT and Microcontroller Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Smart home automation systems employ IoT technologies and microcontrollers to improve security, accessibility, and efficiency in residential spaces. These systems incorporate sensors, actuators, and wireless communication protocols to enable remote monitoring and control of household devices, allowing for enhanced connectivity and seamless operation of various home appliances. This paper conducts a survey on applications in smart home automation focusing on enhancing security, accessibility, and efficiency through IoT and microcontroller integration. Data was systematically collected from Scopus using specific keywords, yielding 49 relevant documents on “Arduino Based Smart Home Automation System” after applying filters for year, subject area, and document type. The abstracts were reviewed, and key details such as issues, methods, and study contexts were summarized for further analysis. Key noticeable aspects in the reviewed literature, include the integration of diverse hardware components such as Arduino boards, Raspberry Pi, and microcontrollers to control home appliances and ensure security. This paper also proposes for research areas that can be further investigated.

articleTitle: Effects of Mechanical Pretreatment Exposure Time on Methane Production in Mono Digestion of WWS and BSY
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The management of organic waste through anaerobic digestion (AD) has emerged as a sustainable solution to energy and sanitation challenges. This study investigates the influence of mechanical pretreatment exposure time on the biomethane potential during the mono-digestion of wastewater sludge (WWS) and brewery spent yeast (BSY). Using a high pressure homogenizer, substrates were subjected to mechanical pretreatment for 5, 10, and 15 minutes. The biochemical methane potential (BMP) was assessed using the AMPTS II setup, and proximate analysis was performed to characterize the substrates. The results indicated cumulative biomethane yields of 15.30, 38.20, and 30.60 Nml for WWS and 38.20, 48.20, and 30.60 Nml for BSY at the respective treatment times. The highest yields were recorded at 10-minute exposure, producing 38.2 Nml and 48.2 Nml of WWS and BSY methane, respectively. These findings highlight the critical role of pretreatment duration in optimizing the AD process for selected feedstocks. The study contributes novel insights into the relationship between mechanical pretreatment and methane production, offering a pathway to enhance the economic viability of anaerobic digestion in organic waste management.

articleTitle: Impact of Loops on the Execution Time of Business Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Loops can be used in business processes to manage repetitive or conditional tasks. Loops, also known as activity repetitions in business processes, have a significant impact on the operational performance of companies. They can have both positive and negative consequences on the process completion time. On one hand, loops are often essential to ensure the quality and satisfaction of tasks. They provide the opportunity to make necessary modifications and verifications, especially in complex processes such as product development or quality checks. However, poor management or excessive use of loops can lead to significant inefficiencies. They increase the overall completion time, resulting in additional expenses and impacting customer satisfaction. For example, when processing orders, repeated revisions can delay delivery, leading to dissatisfaction and financial difficulties. It is crucial to optimize loops to reduce their negative impact. Process mining is an effective approach to represent and study loops, identify gaps, and suggest improvements. It is possible to compare actual processes to ideal models using conformance checking and performance analysis methods to correct discrepancies. This article has provided an opportunity to study the influence of these loops on the total execution time of a business process. By simulating a complex business process, we have demonstrated the impact of overall time on the presence and frequency of loops. The results highlight the importance of improving business process efficiency by optimizing loops.

articleTitle: Comparison of Segregation Indexes and Residential Segregation for Mortality Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Residential racial and economic segregation has been linked to significant disparities in health outcomes, including increased risks for major causes of death. Although the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE) is widely recognized for its robust and comprehensive measure of residential segregation, several other indices, such as the Dissimilarity Index, the Interaction Index, and the Isolation Index, are also commonly employed in segregation studies. However, there is limited research that systematically compares these measures in the context of mortality analysis. This paper seeks to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of various segregation indexes in analyzing the impact of residential segregation on health disparities reflected in mortality rates. Through a detailed analysis of quintiles of ICE and other segregation indexes, we demonstrate that ICE provides a more nuanced and reliable measure for understanding the relationship between segregation and mortality outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of selecting appropriate segregation indexes in public health research and suggest that ICE may be the most effective tool among these residential racial and economic segregations for capturing the complexities of residential segregation's influence on health disparities.

articleTitle: Simulating Scalable Architectures for Cloud Based Systems: Identifying Bottlenecks and Optimal Design Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The rapid increase in demand for cloud services requires strong system architectures that can effectively handle user traffic and adaptively scale to maintain maximum performance and user satisfaction. This research article introduces an innovative simulation model designed to analyze the scalability and dependability of cloud services. Through the utilization of an extensive simulation-based methodology, we replicate user traffic patterns throughout a spectrum spanning from average usage to maximum demands. This enables us to pinpoint any potential bottlenecks that may hinder the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Design and Dynamics Analysis of the Walking System for an Articulated Crawler Tractor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Articulated crawler tractors, with their unique structure and performance, not only have increased capacity compared to traditional tractors but also possess high passing performance and maneuverability. This paper presents the design of the walking systems and a whole-vehicle simulation model for an articulated crawler tractor, enabling research on dynamics simulation. Firstly, the 3D models of track subsystems are established using Recurdyn software. The models are then optimized, which serve as the basis for developing simulation models of the whole vehicle. Subsequently, four simulated terrain conditions, including climbing, step, ditch, and grade E road surface, are created to evaluate the tractor's performance in passing and crossing obstacles under various operational scenarios. Finally, by comparing and analyzing the driving torque, track tension, and vertical acceleration required by the tractor to overcome obstacles, the superiority of the optimized track walking system is verified. Simulation results demonstrate that the optimized track exhibits excellent passing performance, meeting the obstacle-crossing requirements of the tractor while ensuring smoother travel and enhancing driving comfort.

articleTitle: Exploring ResNet50 with Advanced Learning Strategies for Improved Ocular Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Diagnosing retinopathy accurately and promptly from fundus images is crucial, for preventing vision loss and determining the treatment. This study delves into how well deep learning models perform on the Ophthalmic Disease Recognition (ODIR) dataset in categorizing fundus images. Four models were analyzed namely a ResNet50 used as the baseline, ResNet with data augmentation, Bayesian Optimization and Learning Rate Scheduling for hyperparameter fine tuning. After testing the accuracy, sensitivity (recall) and specificity of these models were assessed to uncover their strengths and weaknesses. The Bayesian Optimization model stood out as the most effective achieving a 94% accuracy with excellent sensitivity and specificity. Data Augmentation also proved to enhance performance by enhancing accuracy and sensitivity. The performance boost from both models was statistically significant (at a = 0.05). This research highlights the importance of utilizing optimization methods like Bayesian Optimization to fine tune model hyperparameters for classification outcomes. These insights could have implications beyond retinopathy in medical image classification tasks paving the way for dependable models in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Cancellation of Scattering from Hybrid PB-Metasurfaces with Anti-Phase Sub-Blocks with Generation of Various OAM-Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Wide-angle broadband scattering cancellation from Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) hybrid metasurfaces (MSs) with orbital angular momentum (OAM) is considered. Hybrid MSs are designed from two sub-blocks of different shapes, each of which is a fragment of anti-phase square-shaped OAM-modules. The design was based on a holographic approach. Sub-blocks consist of meta-particles in the form of rectangular patches with cutouts and generate OAM-modes of the same or different orders. The design is based on a holographic approach. Wide-angle diffuse scattering and cancellation of intense co-field side lobes are realized for MSs from sub-blocks generating identical OAM modes, according to the simulation. In the case of an MS from sub-blocks with different OAM-modes, diffusion does not increase; the co-field has intense side lobes in diagonal planes.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Verification Experiment of Solar Thermal Power Generation Device Aiming to Generate Power Exceeding 10mW
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: We have been researching renewable energy. We especially think solar thermal power generation has much potential because the sun shines toward us daily and supplies great thermal power for us. There is no way we do not utilize such energy. Then we started to establish solar thermal power generation devices. In the conventional study, we could fabricate a cone-shaped solar power generation device that can generate several mW. However, we thought that this result was not enough power generation for the size of the device. Another problem with the cone-shaped device was the need for a power unit to direct the concentrator to the sun. To solve these two problems, we have developed a dome-shaped power generation device. The main focus of this device was to eliminate the need for a rotating device by having a dome-shaped light receiving surface, but at the same time, we examined increasing the volume efficiency of power generation. By introducing the light collection coefficient and heat retention coefficient, we were able to clarify the quantitative design guidelines for the device. As a result, the dome-shaped device was able to obtain a coefficient product of about twice that of the cone-shaped device. Finally, we developed an arrayed power generator with dome-shaped devices. We confirmed that an arrayed power generator can generate more than 10mW power with our new test bed which is equipped with a water pool.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study: Predicting Time Series Data with Quantum and Classical Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This research project embarks on a comprehensive comparative analysis of classical and quantum machine learning models specifically tailored for time series forecasting. By employing a range of classical machine learning models alongside quantum machine learning models, the study aims to predict future data points with heightened accuracy and efficiency. Leveraging AWS Braket, the project facilitates the deployment of quantum models on both quantum simulators and quantum hardware devices, providing a robust platform for empirical evaluation. The goal is to meticulously assess the performance metrics, computational efficiency, and predictive accuracy of these models. Ultimately, the research aspires to enhance the understanding and practical application of quantum machine learning techniques in the realm of time series forecasting, potentially uncovering new paradigms in predictive analytics. Our research indicates that the performance metrics for classical machine learning models yielded superior results compared to those of quantum machine learning models for our use case, although when ensembled with classical models, we get better results.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation, and Experimental Implementation of an Electric Vehicle Based on Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The automotive industry has undergone a profound transition towards electric vehicles (EVs), offering a compelling avenue to mitigate global fossil fuel consumption and associated carbon emissions from land transport. While EV charging stations have implications for load management, network stability, and distribution system upgrades, integrating specific solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to power EV battery and motors presents a promising opportunity. In this paper, a model of an electric vehicle powered by a solar modules /DC voltage source, incorporating a battery and motor is proposed. The proposed model uses three switches to control the energy management between the DC source, the battery, and the motor load. In case input DC voltage is available, the DC source will be responsible to change the battery and supply the required the motor receives power from the battery when the input DC voltage is unavailable. Using MATLAB/Simulink, data-driven analysis and simulations validate system performance. Designing a buck converter for voltage control precedes current control to manage battery current. Integration of voltage and current control ensures robust regulation of battery voltage and battery current across diverse conditions. Transitioning to practical implementation involves rigorous testing to verify functionality. Experimental validation confirms the accuracy and functionality of the proposed system and control schemes, contributing to the advancement of EV technology.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Control of a Universal Power Conditioner (UPQC): Application to the Mauritanian Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Harmonics, reactive power, and voltage dips have a detrimental effect on electrical equipment. Several methods such as passive and active filters have been developed to compensate for electrical disturbances, but these methods present difficulties due to the increasing number of non-linear applications. The UPQC (Unified Power Quality Conditioner) is a new topology for resolving load voltage and current imperfections. This article applies UPQC to harmonic elimination, reactive power compensation, and power factor improvement. The technique of reference estimation of instantaneous active and reactive power with a multi-variable filter (FMV-PQ) is used to reduce the number of mathematical calculations. A non-linear control based on the Fuzzy Logic Pulse Width Technique (SVM) is presented to perfectly identify disturbances. Furthermore, a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model has been developed to highlight the effectiveness of the nonlinear control strategy. A range of simulations are performed and examined across different operating conditions. The results obtained show a significant reduction in reactive power, which is decreased by 85%. Both the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the voltage and the harmonic distortion of the current are effectively limited to 0.85%, fully complying with IEEE-519 standards. Furthermore, the compensation of voltage dips proves effective, leading to a notable improvement in the overall power quality.

articleTitle: Bioinspired Cognitive System with Multilevel Task/Subtasks Structure for Autonomous Navigation in Unknown Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The bioinspired cognitive scheme is a distributed processing architecture of three specialized blocks designed to emulate the basic function of the human brain, i.e, memory for generating and storing information about the environment and the state of the system, reason for solving problems in a model of the environment, and motion to execute the solution in the real world. In this paper, to extend the flexibility of this cognitive scheme applied to solve the problem of autonomous navigation in unknown environments with only distance sensors on board, we present an improved cognitive model that introduces the use of a stratified software architecture, where the layers, of decreasing complexity, describes different levels of functions required to displace a mobile robot in a self-discovered horizontal plane by recursive calls of the cognitive scheme. The software layers are organized in a pyramidal structure according to their priority after decompose the tasks in lower level sub tasks and up to basic actions. We introduce the proposed system, first, describing the basic cognitive scheme and then, the stratified software, explaining in particular, the functions designed to explore an unknown environment, to synchronize the real motion with respect to the virtual one, and to navigate in the discovered working space. We illustrate the performance of the system with experimental results obtained using an omnidirectional mobile robot in a horizontal plane.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Diagnosis Techniques for Power Cables: Methods, Applications, and Simulation-Based Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Effective fault detection and diagnosis in power cables play a vital role in maintaining the reliability of power systems. A variety of techniques have been introduced to identify, categorize, and locate faults in both transmission and distribution networks. This study aims to review fault detection and diagnosis techniques for power cables by focusing on methods, applications, and simulation-based validations. The study methodology included a targeted search on Scopus (2019–2023), yielding 49 relevant articles on underground cable fault locators. A bibliographic map with 35 key terms was created using VOSviewer, and the clusters were analyzed, organized in Excel, with key findings documented. Observed review findings includes a wide range of issues relating to fault detection, and distance fault locators for underground cable fault systems. The constant development and implementation of many technologies and approaches to guarantee the precise efficiency of power cable network systems is one important factor that stands out in the literature. This study is crucial as it explores advancements in fault detection for XLPE and subterranean cables, improves fault diagnosis and localization, addresses soft fault detection, and examines challenges in securing submarine cables, along with computational methods for enhanced accuracy in fault detection.

articleTitle: A Scoping Study on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for Effective Decision Making in the Water Management Space in South Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: In many developing countries, wastewater is released into the environment without being tested. The wastewater that is legally discharged to decay never reaches a treatment plant. This has negative impacts on human health, the economy, and the climate change. Previous studies reveal that heavy pollution in the Surabaya River makes the quality of the water bad for people to drink. Similarly, increased industrialisation and urbanisation are studied as sources of pollution and wastewater. The inadequate criteria to measure the quantity and quality of water and its usage patterns have been a significant concern. Though AI is studied in many other domains, very little information is explored in the context of the water sector. The study followed a mixed research design approach. An interview session was conducted with 10 managers and employees working in upper management to have their views on the challenges they face and how AI can help with water management decision-making. For this, snowball sampling was used as it is feasible to generate a pool of participants from acquaintances. Thematic analysis was a valuable tool to generate themes by transcribing responses captured from participants to articulate the findings. Findings show that water companies, policymakers, and the government realise the need to integrate AI and relevant advanced technologies for automation and intelligent outcomes that also aid revenue and profitability. Thus, this research is beneficial in exploring the key challenges met by the water sector in managing the usage, scarcity, quality, and quantity patterns and how AI helps with the management.

articleTitle: Deployment of Demand Response and Battery Energy Storage for Frequency Support in Power System Network with High penetration of Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Among the challenges of high participation of non-fossil energy sources in the generation mix of a power system network is keeping the system frequency nadir within permissible limits during a major power system contingency event. In this work, battery energy storage system and demand response are deployed to offer frequency supports during the loss of the largest single generating unit. Three scenarios of renewable energy penetrations (namely 10%, 30% and 50%) are considered in this work. Simulation results showed that at 10% renewable energy penetration battery energy storage and demand response provided frequency back-up that helped in keeping the frequency nadirs at 59.83Hz and 59.84Hz respectively. Without these supports the frequency nadir would fall to 59.68Hz which is below the acceptable frequency threshold. However, at a high penetration level of 50%, demand response alone could not provide much support (frequency nadir being 59.50Hz) but BESS and combination of BESS and demand response provided sustenance of the frequency nadirs to 59.78 Hz and 59.90Hz respectively.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Management and Optimization in Microgrid Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The growing energy demand from utility customers places significant strain on the power grid, resulting in challenges such as load limitations, power quality issues, and widespread outages. Global energy consumption is expected to increase by more than 50% by 2050, primarily due to the rise in electrification in developing economies. This paper examines the literature related to advanced energy management and optimization in microgrid systems. The research methodology involved a targeted search in the Scopus database, concentrating on literature published between 2022 and 2023 on microgrid integration in power transmission lines. The final analysis utilized VOSviewer to map keyword relationships and trends, identifying key research themes based on clustering keywords with at least four occurrences. The observations indicated that, the power plants, transmission and distribution networks are ageing while maximum demand is on the rise, Microgrid integration to utility grid is a solution to the rising demand of electrical power which puts stress on the existing infrastructure.

articleTitle: The State of Artificial Intelligence Research in SADC Region - A Scientometric Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This article uses scientometrics and text analysis to evaluate the state of artificial intelligence (AI) research in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) region. The Web of Science (WoS) database is searched using over 100 key phrases in the approach that is being used. Additionally, 19 publications that publish artificial intelligence research are included in the search. The years 2013 through 2022 are examined. The major finding is that the SADC region is producing a small number of research publications. Furthermore, the centre of research activity in the field is in South Africa where more than 80% of the relevant research is produced. The main funders of AI research in the region are identified to be in the UK, Europe and China. The productivity of the AI producing organisations in each SADC nation is disclosed upon identification. It is argued that the political neglect of science, technology and innovation in the region is extended even to the field of artificial intelligence which has the potential to advance radically the developmental efforts in the region. It is suggested that collaboration among the research organisations in the region can ameliorate partially the political neglect of R&D in SADC.

articleTitle: Portable Uroflowmetry System with Integrated Software for Home Urinary Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The dynamics of the urinary tract system are important which is an indication of the health of organs in this system. This study presents a portable, low-cost uroflowmetry system designed for home urinary monitoring, capable of detecting lower urinary tract dysfunction through real-time measurements of urine flow rate, voided volume, and voiding time. Early detection of urinary tract problems is crucial for successful treatment, and traditional clinic-based uroflowmetry, though common, can be inconvenient. To address this, an accurate home-based method for repeated uroflowmetry, allowing patients to measure when they are physiologically ready to urinate, is needed. This system used two sensors the load cell and ultrasonic. The results show that the load cell sensor achieved higher accuracy, at 91.11%, compared to 84.44% for the ultrasonic sensor, also precision (0.9285 vs. 0.8450), recall (0.9285 vs. 0.8450), F1 score (0.9284 vs. 0.8449), specificity (0.8823 vs. 0.7290), and MCC (0.8109 vs. 0.6735). Additionally, the load cell sensor produced more accurate measurements across several parameters: Qmax of 13.1 ± 5.5 ml/s, Qavg of 11.9 ± 2.7 ml/s, VV of 280 ± 75.4 ml, VT of 31.6 ± 8.1 seconds, and TF of 21.2 ± 5.5 seconds. In comparison, the ultrasonic sensor produced a Qmax of 10.4 ± 5.8 ml/s, Qavg of 7.3 ± 2.1 ml/s, VV of 320 ± 77.5 ml, VT of 33.8 ± 9.4 seconds, and TF of 26.1 ± 6.8 seconds. Collects urine in real time and analyzes the results, indicating whether the patient suffers from urinary tract disorders. Tested on 45 participants, the system proved effective in providing reliable, repeated measurements in a comfortable home setting, potentially aiding in the early detection and treatment of urinary disorders.

articleTitle: An Overview of Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Measurement Devices Using Microcontrollers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Diabetes is known as one of the most widespread diseases in the world that can affect any age group, from children to older adults. Measuring blood glucose concentration is essential for patients with diabetes, as the result provides confirmation of the need for insulin dose. Commonly used methods to measure glucose levels are invasive for those with the highest accuracy, they cause pain, but also have a higher risk of infection. An alternative, non-invasive is the introduction of pain-free glucose measurement techniques. In this article, some of the devices that could be revolutionary for patients with diabetes are highlighted. The device under investigation employs non-invasive monitoring of blood glucose levels via a glucometer connected to a mobile app, which stores the readings in a database that can be accessed at a later date. This eliminates the need for biological tissue sampling, thereby enhancing the core functionality of the device. Furthermore, the test strips typically utilized in this process are eliminated, reducing both the discomfort associated with the procedure and the overall cost.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Classical Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Machine learning has been on the rise since the 2000's and has gained further prominence since the development of advanced AI chatbots. There have now been clinically accepted prototypes that utilize machine learning in the field of medicine as well. We employ classical machine learning methods to predict for cardiovascular disease presence on a large population of 70000 patients. We further include quantitative and qualitative evaluation with explainability in the prediction of death from standard clinical features. The model establishes diastolic blood pressure and age as the features that contribute most towards cardiovascular disease which is in line with the current expected diagnosis.

articleTitle: Identification and H-Infinity Control for a pH Neutralization Process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental results of the S/KS mixed sensitivity H-Infinity controller implemented in a real pH neutralization plant. For this control system, three variables were considered for control: level, temperature, and pH. To design the H-Infinity controller, linear models for each variable were identified as a first-order plus dead time (FOPDT) transfer function, and a step signal was used to excite each process variable. The system identification process and the design of the H-Infinity controller were implemented using the Matlab toolbox. To begin testing the H-Infinity controller in the real plant, the weight functions were initially defined and then adjusted to ensure robust stability and robust performance for each process variable. The responses of the H-Infinity controller for each variable were compared with those of the PI controller for the same desired reference signals, and the results were satisfactory according to the requirements. In conclusion, we can indicate that the H-Infinity controller is a viable option for use in the industrial processes when the linear model can be obtained.

articleTitle: Automatic Visual Inspection of Granular Biomaterial Under Active Illumination for Accurate Detection of Micro Polluants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: In this paper, to improve the process of quality control in the production line of the biomaterial Nukbone®, we present an Automatic Visual Inspection system with active illumination and an iteractive interface that accurately detects micro pollutants beyond the limits of the human sight and simplify their identification and location for remotion. The system, inspired in the current inspection process that manually detects and remove pollutants off, introduces an illumination strategy to opticaly highlight foreign particles in the sample by integrating numerically filtered images of multiple sources of ligh for enhanced discrimintion properties. It improves real time detection of tiny particles, by contouring them using the Suzuki and Abe method, and displaying the results in a visual interface that shows the inspected sample in a sensible image where, areas with a positive detection are indicated can be selected, to observe, in a magnified image, the detected particles contoured and superimposed on the real image of the biomaterial. We describe the system and its functionality, and illustrate its performance with some examples under real conditions that shows its capacity detecting imperceptible particles in a manual inspection and reducing significatively the inspection time.

articleTitle: Bringing Mechatronic Engineers Closer to the Use of AI Through Generative Design for Manual Power Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Nowadays, several software applications are based on AI algorithms. One of them is the use of Generative Design applications to develop products. This work delves into a practical software application based on AI algorithms to create generative designs for products such as the housing of manual power tools. A case study is used to determine the necessary constraints to design these types of products, and a methodology to create them is described and shared. The results show that the information provided by the software application during the design process is practical and helps develop these types of products; some of this information includes the product mesh representations to be 3D printed, the different design proposals to be selected, and a graphic table where users can compare materials vs. maximum stress. Another result is that the software application is user-friendly and guides the engineers in completing the Generative Design.

articleTitle: ESP32 Library Developed for Petri Net Embedded in RFID Database
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)

authors.preferredName: José J. P. Z. S. Tavares

abstract: This work has the purpose of presenting the expansion of Arduino Library for PNRD (elementary Petri Net inside RFID distributed Database) and iPNRD (inverted PNRD) to ESP32 platform to reach IoT applications. The original Arduino PNRD/iPNRD Library was updated and receipt ESP32 driver to deal with it. In this approach, the Petri Net model is still based on a matrix equation and defined as the data structure of RFID components, which was restructured internally to assist tag data setup. The result is a highly adaptive, distributed, scalable, and applicable control system that allows an automatic exception identification system ready for IoT. Therefore, this work describes the design, implementation, and validation of a library for ESP32 platform which simplifies the development of new applications that use the Arduino PNRD/iPNRD Library.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap: A Comprehensive Analysis of Higher Education Skill Production and Industry Needs in Botswana
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This abstract provides an overview of a study aimed at exploring the disparity between higher education IT skills production and industry needs in Botswana. Despite the significant investments made in higher education institutions in Botswana, concerns have been raised regarding the relevance of the IT skills produced and their alignment with the needs of the rapidly evolving industries. This study sought to identify the root causes of the disparity and suggest potential strategies to bridge the gap. To accomplish this, a qualitative approach was employed. The qualitative phase involved interviews and document review with key stakeholders, including representatives from higher education institutions, industry leaders, and students. These interviews provided valuable insights into perceptions, expectations, and experiences related to the skills gap. The findings of this study were expected to contribute to the existing body of knowledge on the disparity between higher education IT skills production and industry needs in Botswana. By identifying the underlying factors contributing to this mismatch, policymakers, educators, and industry stakeholders would gain a better understanding of the issues at hand and be better equipped to address them. The study also provided evidence-based recommendations and strategies to enhance the alignment between higher education curricula and industry demands, thereby promoting economic growth and development in Botswana. Overall, this research endeavoured to shed light on the complex dynamics between higher education and industry in Botswana, fostering collaboration and synergy between these sectors. By addressing the skills gap, Botswana could strengthen her workforce, enhance competitiveness, and ensure sustainable development in the face of evolving economic demands.

articleTitle: Control Strategies and Battery Management for Hybrid Energy Systems and Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Battery management systems (BMS) play a vital role in enhancing battery performance, ensuring safety, and prolonging lifespan through accurate monitoring, temperature control, and cell balancing. Several energy management strategies have been developed to optimize the distribution of power between energy sources, leading to improved fuel efficiency and better vehicle performance. This paper provides an in-depth review of control strategies and battery management for hybrid energy systems and electric vehicles will be presented. A systematic methodology was employed which involved an extremely thorough and careful approach to identify, select, and evaluate an appropriately connected research documents. The employed methodology included developing of search keywords, search for information from Scopus database, screening and choosing studies based on predefined criteria and synthesizing the findings. This study will examine recent developments in electric vehicle charging, hybrid energy systems, energy harvesting, and solar technologies, focusing on control methods, power conversion, and optimization. It will also explore microcontroller-based systems in energy, robotics, and healthcare. The research will conclude with proposals for future studies, providing direction for ongoing advancements in these areas.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of a Variable-Pitch Axial Flow Fan Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This study performs a multi-objective optimization of a variable pitch fan. The design variables for the optimization considers the camber angle and setting angle of the fan blades, and to calculate the fan's performance and efficiency according to changes in these design variables, a meta model based on CFD modeling is constructed. The design objective functions for the variable pitch fan includes the design point efficiency and the standard deviation between the maximum efficiencies under variable pitch conditions. The optimal design point satisfying the two objective functions is derived from the Pareto front. This optimal design shows an improvement of 3.7 percentage points in design point efficiency compared to the initial design and demonstrated excellent characteristics of maintaining high efficiency over a wide flow rate range, with a standard deviation of 0.76% between the maximum efficiencies under different variable pitch conditions.

articleTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Autonomous SOP Creation: A Methodology for Document Synthesis Across Business Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This Digital Operations for various business functions like Finance & Accounting, Customer Care, Supply Chain Management and others, performed by human operators are extremely reliant on sequential process steps captured in Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). However, the creation of SOPs is highly cumbersome, resource-intensive (cost, time & effort), and time consuming. The motivation of this research is to assist human operators with an autonomous approach for creating baseline SOPs by leveraging existing SOPs in enterprise knowledge corpus. This experimental research aimed at developing a generalized methodology that can ingest SOPs in different formats and generate baseline SOPs in pre-defined business function-specific formats. The research yielded real-world scalable business applications of Retrieval Augmented Generations with Integrated Toolset design pattern at optimal cost. For the production-grade operationalization of such applications, the study focused on a structured approach involved in the selection of search algorithm during the retrieval process. The study mentions the performance of different search algorithms like Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW), Exhaustive K-Nearest Neighbors (X-KNN), and Full-Text search based on evaluation parameters like Latency, Cost and Accuracy. These experimental analyses unfolded the document synthesis system's capability to leverage latent process steps hidden in existing SOPs and reduce the cycle time, operational cost and effort involved in creating SOPs.

articleTitle: State of the Art Survey on Artificial Intelligence-Based Approach for Early Diagnosis of Tuberculosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) has been affecting people and high deaths from it has been recorded globally. Techniques around use of artificial intelligence (AI) based approaches are gaining momentum in early diagnosis of TB. This research has managed to uncover current approaches that are being used in TB diagnosis. It was found out that the AI-based approaches are offering better accuracy especially if the data sets used to train the models are high. Combining various AI-based models was observed to offer better accuracy, i.e., the ensemble approach. The pitfall of the current AI-based models are that they lack interpretability since they are black box and thus cannot offer decision on how the have arrived at the decision, which is a critical area to consider in the medical field. This pitfall can thus be addressed by utilising explainable artificial intelligence, and this has been identified as a future area in this study.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Axial Hydrokinetic Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: In this paper, various types of prototypes of small axial hydrokinetic turbines are presented designed, built and tested in laboratory conditions to prove their operability and efficiency. The hydrokinetic turbines have a diameter of 0.1 m, with a different number of blades and are tested in a free water stream flowing at a velocity of 0,1; 0,2 and 0,3 m/s. Experimental studies are carried out in a specially designed closed-loop laboratory installation or testing prototypes of hydrokinetic turbines. The revolutions of rotation of the turbines are measured. The research includes three measurements: 1. clear stream; 2. with 1 confusor on and 3. with two confusors on in front of the turbine

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of a Hardware Device. A Use Case Study of a Text-to-Braille Translator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: It is imperative to streamline and enhance the daily lives of individuals with visual impairments. One of the most crucial elements of a fulfilling and satisfying existence is the capacity to engage in effective interpersonal communication. Communication between a blind person and a person who is deaf or deafblind can be achieved through a variety of means. One potential solution is the provision of an interpreter, or the use of lip-reading or sign language. This project has developed an alternative method for achieving this without the necessity of another individual's presence. This can facilitate greater independence and a notable enhancement in self-assurance. Moreover, individuals without disabilities have the option of learning Braille in conjunction with their relatives and family members, thereby enhancing their communication with loved ones. The application, which translates words, is straightforward to use and can be utilized by any individual, regardless of age. An analysis of the reliability of the system was conducted based on the developed system to ascertain the traceability of the system's capabilities. A calculation was performed based on the capabilities of the components in order to determine the reliability of the entire system. In light of these considerations, the optimal solution to this problem is the Braille translator, a project that translates text into a readable system for individuals who are blind or deafblind.

articleTitle: Optimizing Quality of Service in WSNs Through Adaptive Node Placement Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are critical in various applications, from environmental monitoring to smart cities. However, optimizing the Quality of Service (QoS) in WSNs remains a challenging task due to the dynamic nature of network environments and resource constraints. This paper proposes an adaptive node placement strategy designed to enhance QoS metrics such as network coverage, energy efficiency, and latency. The strategy dynamically adjusts node positions based on real-time network conditions, ensuring optimal performance even as environmental factors change. Our approach is validated through extensive simulations across various network scenarios, demonstrating significant improvements in QoS compared to traditional fixed node placement methods. The results highlight the potential of adaptive strategies in maintaining robust and efficient WSNs, offering valuable insights for future network designs.

articleTitle: Heat Pattern Design System for a Wire Coil Annealing Process for Specialty Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: When performing heat treatment using a wire coil annealing furnace, it is important to determine the heat pattern that is the target values of the atmosphere temperature in the furnace and the concentrations of CO and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the furnace. However, the response of the furnace atmosphere cannot be predicted and it takes a lot of time to determine the heat pattern. In this study, we developed a design system for heat patterns that can calculate the required flow rate of atmospheric gases during heat treatment by using the proposed furnace atmosphere model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed system was demonstrated by comparing the design results with experimental results.

articleTitle: Investigation of Frequency Response of a Power Network Under Varying Penetration Levels of Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Numerous countries worldwide have prioritized the expansion of renewable energy sources (namely wind and solar photovoltaic) in their energy generation portfolio in order to maintain a healthier environment. Therefore, when the use of renewable energy sources grows, the traditional synchronous-based power generation decreases, leading to a reduction in power system inertia. This is because renewable energy sources do not naturally supply inertia, unless certain reserves are maintained. This study examines the characteristics of the system's frequency behaviors considering varying degrees of renewable energy integration. The study utilized power system software (DIgSILENT Power Factory) to model the IEEE 39-bus test system. The simulation results indicated that when the wind penetration reached 50%, the sudden failure of the largest machine caused a significant increase in rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) of -0.5579 Hz/s. This was in contrast to the ROCOF of -0.3707 Hz/s observed at 0% wind penetration. As a result, the minimum frequency dropped to 59.15Hz, which is below the acceptable threshold of 59.5Hz.

articleTitle: Toward the Development of a Low-Cost AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Auscultation plays a significant role in the screening and clinical diagnosis of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases (CVDs). Experience and domain expertise knowledge are required for accurate diagnosis. However, many resource-constrained countries may not have sufficient expertise. This study, therefore, focuses on the preliminary development and evaluation of a low-cost digital stethoscope which leverages machine learning to distinguish between normal and cardiovascular disease (CVD) related heart sounds. A prototype of a battery-powered digital stethoscope was developed, and the preliminary results showed that the system could capture heart sounds with good quality. Using a PhysioNet Dataset, Machine Learning models (Fine-K-Nearest neighbour FKNN, Gaussian kernel support vector machines GSVMs and Deep Convolutional Neural Networks CNNs) were trained on temporal-frequency derived features of phonocardiogram signals (PCG) by Wavelet scattering and Short-Time-Fast-Fourier Transform (SFFT). The overall validation accuracy range was 89.9%-98.5% and the models could effectively classify normal and abnormal heart sounds. These promising results are essential for screening and the early detection of cardiovascular diseases, enabling timely intervention and disease management in low-resource countries. The work contributes to AI research aimed at enhancing CVD diagnosis and screening.

articleTitle: Pit Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The subject of driving safety is of paramount importance, as it is susceptible to significant risks that can arise from a momentary lapse in attention. In order to achieve this, an application has been developed with the objective of enhancing preventive driving techniques and mitigating the occurrence of adverse events within the context of traffic. The real-time pothole detection application was developed with the objective of assisting drivers in avoiding dangerous road conditions, thus facilitating safe and comfortable driving. The model trained to detect potholes demonstrated robust performance, achieving an average accuracy of 89% and an average recovery rate of 85%. This indicates a high level of ability to correctly classify potholes and identify as many of them as possible. The F1 score, which balances accuracy and retrieval rate, was 0.862, indicating a robust overall performance. The model was trained for a period of nine hours and demonstrated the capacity to effectively identify potholes in a range of conditions. The program is currently capable of detecting potholes on the road, thereby providing a straightforward and efficacious solution for their avoidance.

articleTitle: Semantic Pagewise Augmented Knowledge Retrieval System: SPARKS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of information, the ability to retrieve knowledge effectively from extensive documents has become increasingly critical. Traditional text splitting methods often compromise context and coherency, leading to suboptimal results in knowledge retrieval tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce SPARKS (Semantic and Page-wise Augment Knowledge Retrieval System), a novel approach that leverages semantic segmentation to preserve the contextual integrity of documents. By breaking down documents into semantically coherent chunks rather than arbitrary text blocks, it maintains the narrative flow and thematic continuity, crucial for understanding and querying complex documents. This paper elucidates the benefits of this approach and its potential to redefine knowledge retrieval paradigms.

articleTitle: Application and Use-Cases for a Smart Distribution Grid in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: In response to the pressing issues of climate change and the commitments outlined in the Paris Agreement, there is a global push to increase the share of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in our energy mix. However, these sources fluctuate widely and must be actively controlled to prevent the energy grid from descending into chaos. Smart grids, which are currently being extensively developed worldwide, offer a solution to this challenge. These grids leverage AI optimization algorithms and are made possible by recent advances in embedded microcontrollers and low power modulation techniques. These technological advancements have significantly reduced the cost of the required monitoring solutions, making smart grids a feasible option even for energy systems in developing countries, which are often chaotic. This paper presents a smart grid solution specifically designed for such unorganized energy systems. It is based on a low-cost monitoring installation for the distribution grid that was field-tested in the city of Harar in Eastern Ethiopia. The solution offers a practical approach for imbalance loading and loss analysis, paving the way for more stable and efficient energy systems in developing regions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Thresholding in Document Indexing: An Adaptive Scoring Approach for Retrieval Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: In order to enhance search recall and precision, it is essential to have the capacity to dynamically adjust relevance score thresholds in the constantly evolving field of information retrieval. This research introduces a novel dynamic thresholding paradigm that surpasses static approaches and offers an extensible framework for the Okapi-BM25 retrieval method that can be applied to a variety of datasets. We propose a system design that replicates real-world search scenarios by automatically generating sample queries from newly imported files. The extraction of data segments is directed by these queries, and the scores are statistically analyzed to establish dynamic thresholds by removing outliers and calculating mean scores, among other things. This procedure is a component of a modular system that encompasses scoring, query simulation, data ingestion, and a database administration component that modifies thresholds in response to new data. Utilizing publicly accessible retrieval methodologies and employing Python for statistical analysis, this research demonstrates the capacity of dynamic thresholding to substantially enhance information retrieval results. It provides valuable insights into the practicality and scalability of this approach in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization and Additive Manufacturing of a Loudspeaker Soft Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The advancement of metal additive manufacturing (AM) technologies has enabled the creation of complex geometries for various applications. This paper explores the development of a topology optimized and additively manufactured soft magnetic core for dynamic loudspeakers. By leveraging the synergistic capabilities of topology optimization (TO) and AM, we designed and fabricated a novel loudspeaker core with optimized material utilization. The paper details the modeling, optimization, manufacturing, and initial performance evaluation of the AM loudspeaker core.

articleTitle: Sensitive Voltage Differential Protection Method for Transmission Lines Compensated with SC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: New solar PV and wind generation farms are usually connected to the grid through existing transmission lines, while remote generating plants may be connected through newly constructed long transmission lines (TLs) with limited capacity. In both cases, the power transfer capability of the TLs can be increased by introducing series compensation. Introduction of the series capacitor (SC), however, complicates the protection of the TLs rendering the traditional distance protection ineffective. The literature reports on numerous schemes that are grounded in innovative principles for protection of TLs with series compensation. However, most of the techniques are designed for application with specific compensation points along the line - near end, mid-point or far end. The use of a sensitive voltage differential (SVD) algorithm for the effective protection of a transmission line regardless of the placement of a fixed series capacitor, is suggested in this paper. The algorithm generates a sensitivity-based fault detection index whose magnitude depends on changes in the magnitude and phase of the voltages at the SC and line terminals. The performance of the suggested scheme is evaluated through extensive DigSilent PowerFactory simulations, and the results show that the scheme is sensitive to faults over 100 % of the series-compensated TL and is effectively independent of fault resistance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Retriever Selection in RAG Systems: An RL Approach to User-Centric NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This paper investigates a novel use of Reinforcement Learning (RL) to dynamically choose the best retriever in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems with the goal of improving the performance of natural language processing tasks. RAG systems combine retrieval techniques with pre-trained language models to produce responses that are accurate within their context, but a static retriever selection system results in inefficiencies, in a dynamically changing environment where user preferences and the document corpus evolves. We attempt to solve this problem by proposing an RL-based solution to enable dynamic retriever selection based on document context and user feedback. The reinforcement learning agent is able to adjust to user preferences and a changing document corpus by utilizing Q-Learning. The methodology covers issue formulation, agent architecture and training procedures. Our experiments validate our RL-based approach's performance characterized by metrics like user satisfaction and response accuracy. The discussion highlights the strengths and limitations of the Reinforcement Learning approach and suggests future research directions. This experiment underlines the potential of adaptive mechanisms in NLP, showcasing RL's capability to revolutionize RAG applications by creating more responsive and user-tailored NLP systems. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Innovative Adapter-Based Fine-Tuning and Streamlined Training Strategies for Text Summarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This research paper investigates efficient fine-tuning techniques for Large Language Models (LLMs) with a focus on minimizing computational costs and memory usage. We explore various Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) approaches, including Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations (IA)3, and Prompt Tuning, to evaluate their performance and feasibility in adapting open-source language models for text summarization without compromising effectiveness. By integrating DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 Offload and Flash Attention, we enhance memory utilization and accelerate training, achieving a 30-35% reduction in training time and a 15-20% decrease in GPU memory consumption. Our findings indicate that (IA)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and Prompt Tuning give comparable performance to LoRA while using much lesser parameters while training. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of PEFT techniques of different nature and their potential impact on optimizing large language models when combined with efficient training strategies, making them more accessible for consumer with less hardware resources while maintaining good performance.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Displacement Measurement Experiment Using Self-Mixing Laser Diode Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This paper presents the design and evaluation of a laser-based relative dynamic displacement measurement using the self-mixing laser diode technique. A 980-nm wavelength near infrared laser diode was driven under constant current regime, while the monitor photodiode current was processed by a transimpedance amplifier to allow detection and recording of the interference pattern due to the oscillation of a target (loudspeaker diaphragm) located just in front of the laser diode package. Several experiments were carried out, by changing the frequency and amplitude of the target oscillation. In spite of the instrumentation simplicity, the interference patterns recorded for every experiment made its adequacy clear enough.

articleTitle: Engineering and Data-Driven Approaches for Load Forecasting: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Precise load forecasting is critical for ensuring the equilibrium between electricity supply and demand, reducing operational costs, and optimizing resource scheduling in power systems. In this study, a comprehensive literature review on the engineering and data-driven approaches for load forecasting is conducted. A systematic review was performed using the Scopus database, narrowing down 635 initial results through filtering. VOSviewer software was utilized to analyze keyword relationships, revealing major themes and potential areas for further research. The literature reviewed highlights two primary categories of load forecasting methods: engineering (or physics-based) models and data-driven (or AI-based) models. Engineering methods utilize thermodynamic principles and detailed contextual data, such as building structure and HVAC systems, to estimate energy consumption, as demonstrated in software like EnergyPlus and eQUEST.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Non-Linear Low Pass Filter, Compromising of an RF Signal Generator Used as a Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This study describes a low-pass RF signal transmitter that rejects sideband frequencies to produce carrier frequency. The RF compromises of a RF Amplify module (RFA), a Mixer Module (MM), a Local Oscillator (LO), RF Filter and an Antenna. The mixer performance is adopted to mix an IF signal with a local oscillator in creating a sum and difference. Moreover, this is a nonlinear mixer. The transmitter elliptic filter provides a minimum of 30 dB of attenuation at the local oscillator frequency from the mixer and a minimum of 30 dB of attenuation on the unwanted sideband frequency from the mixer. The paper focuses on the design and simulation of a transmitter. The purpose of this design is to convert an IF signal to a radio frequency signal by frequency mixing, which travels long distances upon transmission.

articleTitle: Energy Security Analyses at the Black Sea in the New Context of Insecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Any analysis of vulnerabilities, risks and threats to the security of a state must start from a simple reality - global hydrocarbon reserves are gradually being reduced, and other energy powerful states continue to remain the main sources of energy deficit coverage. Bulgaria, like other european countries, it is and remains dependent on the import of energy resources only if no new important oil and gas deposits will be discovered and exploited at the Black Sea, nuclear and renewable energy will not gain a greater share in the energy mix, investment in the national energy industry will not increase and EU energy policy is pushing for the closure of coal-fired power plants. To these are added the generally high prices that Moscow practices, through Gazprom, for oil and gas deliveries to the European market or other threats less relevant to our analysis. Therefore, the most important threat that can have a critical impact on the national economy and the objectives of economic and social development and security is the reduction/sistration of hydrocarbon supplies from external sources. To this is added certain actions of foreign companies to ensure control over some national energy resources, production and distribution capacities or other critical infrastructure in the energy field, which may have a marginal impact on the development of the Romanian economy and society. The authors set out to analyse Bulgaria's state of energy security (hydrocarbon resources, coal, gas and electricity security supply) and to find optimal variants that would bring about a substantial improvement in national security and good living.

articleTitle: Cutting-Edge Predictive Methods for Enhancing Short-Term Load Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Efficient management and cost-related factors in the power sector call for accurate short-term load forecasting as it enables better planning with the electric grid and achieving stability within it. This paper looks into the state-of-the-art forecasting strategies that enhance load forecasts made in shorter time frames. Such techniques include but are not limited to machine learning applications, effective data models, and multi-dimensional modeling leveraging historical, meteorological, and economic data. Their review is carried out in detail with their advantages and disadvantages and their application in practice. Furthermore, this study strives to understand the barriers that need to be overcome in the quest to increase the accuracy of the forecasting models especially concerning renewable energy sources. We illustrate how new trends relate to future developments of predictive models about supporting the decision-making in operating power systems and improving the reliability and sustainability of energy systems.

articleTitle: A Graph Based Framework for Removing Outliers in Time Series Boolean Signals: A Case Study of an Automatic Door
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: A dataset is a collection of data items gathered from various but related sources. A dataset's instance is known as a data record and can be characterised by several data attributes known as features. Today, data has become a fuel in everyday life as well as for artificial intelligence-based models for decision-making, learning, and automation. Many devices, such as sensors, cameras, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, can be used to collect data. If there are any inconsistencies in the collected data, the outputs of traditional algorithms or models based on artificial intelligence could be negatively affected. In this paper, we have proposed a novel transition-based graph model for handling outliers in time series boolean signals. Our proposed model detects and removes the outliers from the time series boolean signals. We have simulated time series boolean signals for an automatic door and verified that our proposed model can successfully remove the outliers. Our proposed model can be used to remove outliers in situations where predictive maintenance will be carried out based on time series boolean signals,

articleTitle: Enhancing the Security of Public Key Cryptography in Addressing Quantum Computing Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The potential of quantum computing to compromise traditional public-key cryptography (PKC) has led to a pressing need for more efficient and resilient cryptographic methods. Recent advancements, such as the 800x improvement in the logical error rate by Microsoft and QUANTINUUM, underscore the urgency of this issue. Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) offers a promising solution designed to withstand quantum attacks. This paper examines how PQC and other advanced cryptographic techniques can enhance the security and efficiency of PKC in the quantum era. Current PKC methods, despite revolutionizing secure online communication, are vulnerable to flaws in their underlying algorithms. The proposed hybrid model integrates PQC with traditional PKC, leveraging both technologies' strengths to mitigate quantum threats while preserving established security benefits. The investigation addresses critical research questions: how to enhance PKC key management for better efficiency and security, and which PQC techniques can protect PKC from quantum attacks. This paper's contribution includes identifying vulnerabilities in existing PKC, comparing RSA and post-quantum algorithms, and implementing a PQC algorithm between a client and server to analyze integration with existing protocols. Finally, the paper recommends security mechanisms to improve PQC protocols, ensuring robust protection against emerging quantum computing capabilities.

articleTitle: Blockchain in Logistics and Smart City Transportation: A Hyperledger Fabric-Focused Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Blockchain technology is transforming multiple sectors by tackling challenges in data transparency, security, and operational efficiency. This literature review centers on Hyperledger Fabric's role within logistics and smart city transportation, exploring how it addresses issues like data silos, transparency gaps, and security risks common in these fields. Drawing on recent advancements and case studies, the review illustrates how Hyperledger Fabric enhances data transparency and traceability, reinforces stakeholder security, and boosts operational efficiency and cost savings. Through comparative analysis with platforms such as Ethereum and R3 Corda, Hyperledger Fabric's advantages in scalability, modularity, and privacy emerge, showing why it's well-suited to industrial applications. Findings reveal Hyperledger Fabric's strong integration capabilities and support for complex smart contracts as essential benefits for logistics and urban transport. Yet, the study also notes challenges like scalability, interoperability, and setup costs, while suggesting potential solutions. It further examines how progress in one sector can benefit the other, fostering cross-industry innovation. This review offers practical insights for researchers, industry professionals, and policymakers interested in leveraging blockchain to transform logistics and urban transportation, underscoring the importance of continued research to address adoption barriers. With its specialized features, Hyperledger Fabric demonstrates strong potential to meet these sectors' evolving demands.

articleTitle: Context-Aware Sentiment Analysis in Setswana
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Sentiment analysis traditionally faces significant challenges in low-resource languages, primarily due to the lack of robust, annotated datasets and tools tailored to specific linguistic contexts. This paper addresses these challenges within the Setswana language by leveraging its unique cultural and linguistic attributes that influence sentiment expression. We present a novel adaptation of transformer-based models, specifically PuoBERTa, bert-base-multilingual-cased, XLM-Roberta, afro-xlmr-base, multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1, and setu4993/LaBSE, enhanced with contextual hints.
