That affects the availability of resources during infrastructure deployment using attacks such as DoS attacks, injection attacks, Man in the Middle (MITM), malware spread, remote code execution (RCE), and phishing attacks to penetrate the cloud infrastructures. The paper aims to analyze Terraforms infrastructure as code in cloud security to fortify codes and assist DevSecOps engineers in identifying misconfiguration in Terraform scripts. The paper's contributions are threefold. First, we explore cloud security by securing IaC solutions on Terraform. We consider security issues, including misconfigurations and coding errors, present in Terraform IaC. Secondly, we implement a static analysis tool for terraform by comparatively analyzing existing tools. Finally, we provide a comparative analysis of terraform IaC on tools including Checkov, Tfsec, Tflint, and Terrascan for suitability based on their key features and performance metrics to enhance security.

articleTitle: Elastic Blockchain Security Solution for Edge Computing Supporting Mobile IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: When integrated, blockchain technology and cloud computing (EC) may improve security and protect data. However, when data is sent to EC, the Internet of Things (IoT) device layer cannot guarantee data security. As a result, in the IoT ecosystem, end users and IoT devices are susceptible to assaults. Additionally, as the number of IoT devices rises and generates a large quantity of data, especially in mobile IoT devices, security concerns rise dramatically. High security and privacy standards are necessary for industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications in order to safeguard data and guarantee that IoT devices may seamlessly switch to another network. By utilising its decentralised structure, consensus process, and encryption features, blockchain technology can offer a solution. However, because IIoT devices have limited resources, the encryption procedure might be complicated. Actually, in order to secure communication between IIoT devices and EC, this research suggests a new security mechanism built on blockchain technology. Additionally, two security tiers will be used by the Elastic Blockchain Security Solution (EBC) to create a dynamic system for mobile IIoT devices. To evaluate the EBC solution's effectiveness, scalability, and performance, as well as its consensus method and encryption capabilities, it was put into practice and tested in a number of scenarios

articleTitle: Designing a Code Obfuscation Scheme for Software Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Software piracy and intellectual property theft has brought about a financial decrease in revenue for the producers of software systems. Moreso, malicious end-users act as Man-At-The-End (MATE) attackers and dangerously inspect software codes either statically or dynamically to steal them. Developers need to create client applications that contain confidential information and data. As a result, large scale software firms constantly strive to secure hidden algorithms and vital programming components contained in their applications in order to have competitive advantage. The focus of this study is to design a code obfuscation scheme for software and intellectual property protection. The methodology employed includes use of programming tool and algorithms that described the key processes of the scheme. To demonstrate the strength and capability of our approach, user evaluation was conducted to arrive at the cost, potency and resilience of the scheme. Results indicate that majority of the respondents believe that the developed obfuscator is inexpensive and that it does not adversely affect memory and execution time. The current study would provide software developers the tool to obscure their intellectual property against theft.

articleTitle: Research on the Indicators for Ageing Adaptation of Community Evaluation System Under the Concept of Dementia Friendly
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Objective: Under the key issue of community aging transformation, it is an inevitable trend to explore in depth to provide effective guidance for the independent travel of the elderly with early dementia under the community pension model, which is to maintain the physical and mental health of the elderly and promote the development of healthy aging. Methods: Taking the renovation of the signage system in the community environment as an entry point and guided by the “dementia-friendly” theory, this study divides the renovation indicator system into seven major criteria: spatial guidance, safety, auxiliary functions, sensory stimulation, socialization, meaningful participation, and sustainable development, ultimately selecting 43 indicators as operational renovation indicators. A large community in Xi'an was used as a case study. A combination of interview methods and life trace recording techniques was employed to capture the behavioral characteristics of the elderly's daily activities within the community. Additionally, an importance comparison matrix and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) were used to construct the evaluation system's structural model, thereby establishing an indicator weight judgment matrix. Results: A method for constructing age-friendly renovation indicators for community signage systems under the “dementia-friendly” concept was proposed. Conclusion: These indicators can serve as a theoretical foundation for future research on age-friendly renovations in community environments for elderly individuals with early-stage dementia and disabilities.

articleTitle: Before We Disappear: The New Faces of Interactive Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: Interactive films offer a novel viewing experience that diverges from traditional linear cinema. This paper presents an ethical approach to creating an adaptive interactive film using facial recognition software for emotion detection without personal data collection. We propose a new algorithm that dynamically determines scene order based on viewers' emotional responses, ensuring varied experiences across multiple screenings while maintaining narrative coherence. Our method addresses ethical concerns surrounding data protection and AI use in media. Quantitative analysis shows 91.5% facial recognition accuracy in cinematic environments and 87.6% viewer engagement rates. Initial testing demonstrates significant improvements in scene order generation and viewer satisfaction compared to traditional interactive films. This research contributes to the growing field of affective computing in interactive media, exploring the balance between personalisation and privacy.

articleTitle: The Development of a Community Microgrid Psychosocial Governance Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: This study addresses the gap in research on the institutional governance structures of community microgrids, particularly from a network governance perspective and broader psychosocial factors influencing user participation. It integrates Network Governance Theory and the Theory of Planned Behaviour to develop a conceptual framework for inclusive governance in community microgrids, grounded in the belief that governance structure precedes operational or managerial action. Data was gathered through a seven-point Likert scale questionnaire distributed via WhatsApp in Milnerton, Cape Town, with 113 responses. The study's theoretical contribution lies in the novel integration of the two theories, identifying five crucial variables and developing a framework tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). This testing confirmed the framework's reliability and validity, demonstrating high explanatory and predictive power. Empirical findings reveal significant relationships between prosumers' attitudes towards community microgrids, perceived inclusive control, and their intentions to support inclusive governance, mediated by their willingness to participate. Specific hypotheses were tested, showing significant relationships between attitudes and intentions to participate, and between perceived control and both intentions to participate and willingness to adopt network governance. This study uses a pure quantitative research method. By utilizing SEM and SmartPLS 4 software, it provides a substantial methodological contribution to the literature on community microgrids, demonstrating the effectiveness of SEM in this context. This study significantly enhances the literature by offering a robust, empirically validated network governance framework for community microgrids.

articleTitle: Mechanical Pre-Treatment of Co-Digested Wastewater Sludge (WWS) and Brewery Spent Yeast (BSY) Under Anaerobic Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER)
abstract: The food and beverage industries produce vast amounts of organic residue with the potential for biogas production. Among others, mechanical pre-treatment could be a useful option that enhances the biomethane yield of brewery-spent yeast and wastewater sludge. Therefore, this study investigates the co-digestion of brewery-spent yeast and wastewater sludge via mechanical pre-treatment to improve the biomethane yield. The co-digestion was carried out in 1: 2 of wastewater sludge to brewery spent yeast. A high-pressure homogenizer was used to mechanically pre-treat the WWS and (BSY) with 5-, 10-, and 15-minute exposure times. The proximate analysis was carried out, and biomethane potential was measured using the BMP AMPTS 11 setup. This study noticed a tremendous increase in biomethane yields compared to mono digestion; this can be traced to the co-digestion with wastewater sludge. The effect of co-digestion can be inferred to be more effective in the treatment with the best pre-treatment conditions. The treatment with 10 min exposure time released the highest volume of 175.30 Nml biogas. This can be traced to pre-treatment methods that have made the substrate accessible to biomethane-produced microorganisms. The pre-treatment improved the substrate's surface area, enabling sufficient interaction between the wastewater sludge, substrate, and microbes. Finally, this result shows the significant impact of mechanical pre-treatment, which is more noticeable than the effect of co-digestion.
